Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking a minute — I'm Samir (Head of Platform at SupplyWise). We're evaluating hosted inference providers for a PoC to power an internal knowledge assistant and a customer-facing insights dashboard. Two quick asks to start:

1) Baseline per-1M token pricing broken out by input vs. output (we want to model costs precisely).
2) A short catalog/list of hosted models you offer (names + guidance on latency / recommended max sequence length for each).

For context: expected initial volume ~30M tokens/month, mostly short queries (avg 200 tokens) but some long-form generation spikes during reports (up to 2k tokens). Use case is retrieval-augmented generation + moderate safety filtering.

Also: do you publish committed-volume discount tiers or is that only via reserved capacity/Dedicated? Any example thresholds/discounts (e.g., 50M, 200M) and whether IO split matters to tiering would be helpful.

If you can send a one-page baseline and a model roster we can share internally. Happy to hop on a quick call this week if needed.

Best,
Samir

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear context, this is exactly the kind of detail that helps. Looping Ben (our pricing lead) to cover committed discounts and reserved options.

Quick baseline (hosted API, USD, per 1M tokens) — input / output listed separately to make modeling straightforward:

- Redwood-compact (small retrieval / embeddings-friendly): input $12 / output $24 per 1M tokens
- Redwood-mid (general-purpose text, balanced latency): input $40 / output $80 per 1M tokens
- Redwood-xl (larger-context generation optimized for quality): input $110 / output $220 per 1M tokens

Notes: these are baseline hosted rates for multi-tenant capacity. We also have quantized model variants (same model family, smaller binary footprint) that are roughly 35% cheaper on token rates and are a common cost-saver for high-volume RAG workloads.

Model roster (short):
- Redwood-compact: 2k recommended max seq; median p95 latency ~45ms (per 512-token request)
- Redwood-mid: 4k recommended max seq; median p95 latency ~120ms (per 512-token request)
- Redwood-xl: 8k recommended max seq; median p95 latency ~300ms (per 512-token request)

If you have a specific latency SLO or spike pattern we can recommend an optimal model/quantization mix.

Volume discount examples (hosted API):
- 10% off list at 50M paid tokens/month
- 18% off at 200M paid tokens/month
- Custom pricing (25%+) for >1B with a committed 12-month program or Reserved/Dedicated contract

IO split: by default discounts apply to the aggregate billed tokens (input+output). For highly output-heavy workloads we sometimes model tiering on output-dominant usage and can offer transient credits for early-stage spikes.

I've attached a short draft ratecard with the above numbers plus an outline of Reserved capacity (Dedicated) benefits and a sample commitment discount schedule. If that looks reasonable I can follow up with a clean quote/statement of work.

Attachment: RW-hosted-baseline-ratecard-draft-20270821.pdf (one-pager, draft)

Would you like a formal quote (PDF) or a draft MSA + SOW to share with your procurement team?

Thanks,
Priya

Hi Samir / Priya — Ben here. Thanks Priya for the draft. Samir: a couple operational points that typically matter to customers at your scale and might affect the economics:

- Committed vs. Reserved: If SupplyWise prefers fixed predictability we can surface a Dedicated Reserved SKU with slightly better unit economics (example: additional 8-12% off baseline for 6–12 month commitments depending on GPU mix).
- Ramp windows: we can build a tiered ramp (e.g., 3-month trial at baseline list, month 4–6 at 10% discount, then full committed tier) to reduce initial cash/commitment friction.
- Trial credits: we can offer a $10k hosted credit to run parallel RAG tests for two weeks — common for PoCs.

I've attached a simple discount schedule template that shows examples for month-to-month vs committed deals. If you can share a target monthly committed token number and preferred start date I can sketch an official quote and a reserved/Dedicated comparison.
